summary:
Radar for 2026-10-06 (GLP-1 focus). The post-EASD news wave has moved from headline efficacy numbers to three things: muscle quality, side effects people can search for, and benefits beyond weight. The best early opportunities are:
(1) Regeneron's trevogrumab COURAGE phase 2. Adding it to semaglutide cut lean-mass loss to 4.2% vs 7.3% at 52 weeks. It's a muscle-pillar story that hasn't been peer reviewed yet and has little creator coverage.
(2) The Wegovy/NAION vision-loss story (KXAN, syndicated to Yahoo Oct 5). It's a named-drug safety question, and we can calmly decode it with EMA's 'very rare' figure.
(3) NYU's Mendelian-randomization study linking GLP-1 to male-pattern hair loss (Washington Post Oct 3). It's a searchable named-drug side effect, and honesty works here because the evidence is genetic proxies, not a trial.
(4) Wake Forest's piece on why GLP-1 lowers 'wanting' rather than 'liking'. It fits our #1 Short formula (a named-drug mechanism question, honest about animal data).
(5) Taltz + Zepbound in psoriasis (TOGETHER-PsO): 27.1% vs 5.8% reached both clear skin and ≥10% weight loss. It's a benefit beyond weight with a named comparator.
Seasonal: Halloween on a GLP-1 (People.com is already covering it) peaks in about 3 weeks.
Carry-overs still accelerating: the conception/pregnancy meta-analysis (86), plus postpartum prescriptions and the paediatric data (Pediatrics prescriptions for ages 8–11 and the Childhood Obesity study on nutritional deficiencies). These are for caution-level 'parents ask' content only.
Survodutide SYNCHRONIZE-2 (NEJM) is strong news, but we already covered it in long-form on 10-05. Only re-use it as an estimand-decoder Short.
Peaking items (retatrutide approval searches, tirzepatide vs semaglutide 'best drug 2026') need a differentiated decoder angle.
Rejected: the GLP-1 'microdosing' trend (Yahoo, Oct 6). It breaks the no-microdosing guardrail.

candidates.topic: Trevogrumab + semaglutide: lean-mass loss 4.2% vs 7.3% on semaglutide + placebo at 52 weeks (Regeneron phase 2 COURAGE, 75 mg arm; investigational, not yet peer reviewed)
candidates.angle: 'Can a muscle drug stop semaglutide taking muscle?' Decode the 42% headline: what it means in absolute terms (4.2% vs 7.3% of lean mass). The 25 mg dose wasn't significant. It's investigational and only available in trials. Then pivot to what works today: protein (unless your clinician has told you to limit it, e.g. kidney disease) and strength training. Say it's company-reported conference data, not a peer-reviewed paper.
keywords: how to keep muscle on Wegovy
candidates.why_now: Regeneron's final COURAGE results came out ~Oct 1 and Medical Daily/inc.com picked them up Oct 3–4. Muscle loss is one of the most-searched GLP-1 worries, and the Lancet women's review (Sep 29) separately flags lean-mass loss, so the theme is reinforced from two sources. Few creator videos so far.

evidence.signal: Phase 2 COURAGE confirms trevogrumab reduces lean-mass loss during semaglutide-induced weight loss
Trevogrumab cuts semaglutide-associated lean-mass loss by about half
4.2% vs 7.3% lean-mass loss at 52 weeks; 25 mg not significant; not peer reviewed

candidates.topic: Semaglutide and sudden vision loss (NAION): an Austin father's Wegovy story vs what regulators say (EMA: very rare side effect, up to 1 in 10,000 users; causation still debated)
candidates.angle: 'Can Wegovy affect your eyesight?' Calm decoder. What NAION is (a 'stroke' of the optic nerve, painless loss of vision in one eye). Shared risk factors (diabetes, high blood pressure, sleep apnea). EMA's 2025 'very rare' conclusion. What studies disagree on. Red flag: sudden vision change means same-day urgent care, and tell your prescriber. Don't stop medication on your own. Fact-checker must verify the current FDA label status before stating it.
candidates.why_now: The KXAN story (Oct 5) was syndicated on Yahoo the same day, and a 'fda adds new warning to weight loss drugs including wegovy' search query is circulating. Fear-driven searches are spiking, and law-firm pages dominate the results, so there's room for a balanced, evidence-led answer.

evidence.signal: Austin father loses vision in one eye after Wegovy; NAION link being studied, causation not proven
Mainstream pickup Oct 5

candidates.topic: Semaglutide and male-pattern hair loss: NYU Mendelian-randomization study links genetically higher GLP-1 receptor expression to androgenetic alopecia (J Invest Dermatol; Washington Post Oct 3)
candidates.angle: 'Can semaglutide cause male-pattern baldness?' Honest answer: this study used genetic proxies (22 variants), not people on the drug. Contrast it with the far commoner temporary shedding after rapid weight loss (telogen effluvium) and the BMJ 2026 rates (~7 vs 4–5 per 1,000 per year in T2D). End with when to see a dermatologist.
candidates.why_now: The Washington Post wellness piece (Oct 3) came after earlier ScienceDaily, Newsweek and ScienceAlert coverage, so the claim is already circulating. Hair loss is one of the most-searched GLP-1 side effects, and the 'genetic proxy, not trial' nuance is mostly missing from coverage.

evidence.signal: New study suggests possible connection between GLP-1s and hair loss in men
Ozempic and Wegovy may raise hair loss risk in some men (NYU Langone)
Mendelian randomization; not proof of causation

candidates.topic: Why semaglutide quiets 'food noise': GLP-1 lowers 'wanting' (dopamine-driven drive) more than 'liking' (pleasure), per Wake Forest's reward-system research (mostly animal studies)
candidates.angle: 'Does Ozempic make food less enjoyable?' Search-style mechanism question. The nucleus accumbens and dopamine, explained simply. The wanting vs liking split. Mark clearly which findings are rodent-only and which come from human imaging. Close with practical habits: eating slower and stopping at comfortable fullness.
keywords: does Ozempic make food taste different
candidates.why_now: Wake Forest published this on Oct 5. Neuroscience News and a Frontiers paper add supporting coverage. It fits our best-performing Short format (a named-drug mechanism question that answers honestly, 'only in animals so far': 113 views).

evidence.signal: What the neuroscience of motivation has to say about GLP-1 drugs (Oct 5)
GLP-1 drugs engage hindbrain–amygdala–dopamine circuit reducing motivation for high-calorie food
Supporting review on GLP-1 and reward

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide + ixekizumab for psoriasis with obesity: 27.1% reached complete skin clearance AND ≥10% weight loss vs 5.8% on ixekizumab alone at 36 weeks (TOGETHER-PsO phase 3b, Lilly)
candidates.angle: 'Can tirzepatide help psoriasis?' Benefit beyond weight with a named comparator. PASI 100: 40.6% vs 29.0%. Average BMI >39. Add context from the Clin Dermatol review (Oct 1) and the JEADV hidradenitis suppurativa cohort (Oct 3). Lilly-funded trial, open about the population; tirzepatide is not approved for psoriasis.
candidates.why_now: New data on Oct 5 (EADV season), plus fresh PubMed reviews on psoriasis (Oct 1) and HS (Oct 3). Dermatology plus GLP-1 is an underserved search niche with a sizable audience (psoriasis tracks with obesity).

evidence.signal: Taltz + Zepbound superior to Taltz alone in TOGETHER-PsO (27.1% vs 5.8% composite)
GLP-1 receptor agonists in psoriasis management (Oct 1)
GLP-1 RAs in hidradenitis suppurativa: nationwide cohort (Oct 3)

candidates.topic: Halloween on a GLP-1: why sweets and fatty treats may sit differently on semaglutide or tirzepatide (slower gastric emptying, nausea triggers) plus portion-friendly swaps
candidates.angle: 'Halloween candy on Mounjaro or Ozempic: what to expect.' Upbeat and practical, with no restriction or shame. Covers smaller portions, pairing treats with protein, eating slowly, and why greasy, very sweet foods can worsen nausea for some people. Positive framing: enjoy the holiday. Avoid extreme-diet messaging.
candidates.why_now: People.com published '8 Halloween Treats You'll Still Love While Taking a GLP-1' on Oct 5, so the seasonal cycle is starting now. Publishing in the next 1–2 weeks lets content rank before the Oct 31 peak.

evidence.signal: 8 Halloween Treats You'll Still Love While Taking a GLP-1 (Oct 5)
Expert review of GI adverse effects of GLP-1 and GIP/GLP-1 agonists (Oct 2026)

candidates.topic: Women on semaglutide or tirzepatide: Lancet Obstetrics, Gynaecology & Women's Health review flags lean-mass loss (~30% of weight lost commonly lean mass) and nutrient gaps (vitamin D, iron, magnesium, potassium, choline)
candidates.angle: '5 nutrients to ask your doctor about on Wegovy or Zepbound (women).' Supportive and practical: why intake drops early, which nutrients the review flags, plus protein and resistance training. Frame it as 'commonly reported in body-composition studies', not a fixed rule. Women are most GLP-1 users, yet guidance lags behind.
candidates.why_now: The Lancet review came out Sep 29, with Nutritional Outlook coverage on Oct 6 and Medical Xpress earlier. It also lines up with the paediatric nutrient-deficiency study, making 'nutrition on GLP-1' a converging theme.

evidence.signal: Lancet review flags lean-mass loss and access barriers for women on GLP-1s
Women are and will be predominant GLP-1 users, research gaps remain

candidates.topic: GLP-1 exposure around conception: no clearly detectable increase in miscarriage, birth defects or preterm birth (meta-analysis of 10 studies, ~2.1M pregnancies, 8,325 exposed) + French nationwide T2D pregnancy safety study (Diabetologia)
candidates.angle: 'Got pregnant on semaglutide or tirzepatide: what does the evidence say?' Reassuring but exact: 'no clearly detectable increase' is not 'proven safe'. Few exposed pregnancies; observational data. Current labels advise stopping before planned pregnancy, so talk to your prescriber; don't change medication on your own. Note oral contraceptive interaction with tirzepatide only if verified.
candidates.why_now: Momentum rose from 76 to 86 across snapshots. Medical Xpress and the Pharmaceutical Journal covered it on Oct 5, and Diabetologia's French study adds a second source. 'Ozempic babies' is a long-running viral question.

evidence.signal: No detectable increase in pregnancy risks after GLP-1 exposure around conception, largest review to date
Safety of GLP-1 RAs and new glucose-lowering agents for T2D in pregnancy: French nationwide study

candidates.topic: Survodutide decoder: why the same NEJM trial says 13.1% (efficacy estimand, 6.0 mg) AND 9.8% (treatment-regimen) vs placebo 3.1%/3.9% at 76 weeks in adults with overweight or obesity + type 2 diabetes (SYNCHRONIZE-2)
candidates.angle: Short-only follow-up to the 10-05 long-form: 'Did survodutide lose 13% or 10%? Both, and here's why.' Teaches estimands using a named drug. A1C down up to 1.21 points from 7.4%. Use the paper's participant count, not the press release's. Any tirzepatide comparison must be framed as cross-trial, not head-to-head.
candidates.why_now: The NEJM publication (Oct 1) and the Contemp Clin Trials review are driving coverage across Healio, AJMC and HCPLive. Consumer creators haven't explained the two estimands yet. Note: our L1 already covered survodutide on 10-05, so use this only as a differentiated Short.

evidence.signal: Survodutide Once Weekly in Adults with Obesity and Type 2 Diabetes
Treatment-regimen −8.2%/−9.8% vs −3.9% placebo at 76 weeks
Up to 13.1% weight loss in T2D (efficacy estimand)

candidates.topic: How semaglutide may protect kidneys: Nature Medicine biopsy RCT (106 adults with T2D + CKD, 52 weeks): MRI primary endpoints unchanged vs placebo, but kidney-tissue signals point to healthier blood vessels and less inflammation
candidates.angle: 'How does semaglutide protect your kidneys?' Start with the outcome evidence (FLOW). Then add this mechanism trial and report its null primary result exactly: 'not significantly changed', secondary/exploratory transcriptomics. Population: adults with T2D and CKD.
candidates.why_now: Published in Nature Medicine on Oct 1, plus an Australian multidisciplinary panel paper on semaglutide in T2D + CKD (Intern Med J, Sep 30). No consumer coverage yet, so it suits a benefits-beyond-weight piece with a named drug and named comparator.

evidence.signal: Effects of semaglutide on kidney disease in type 2 diabetes: a randomized placebo-controlled trial
Semaglutide in T2D and CKD in Australia: practical considerations

candidates.topic: 'Ozempic nails': nail detachment self-reported by 39.3% of GLP-1 users vs 8.7% of controls (EADV online survey, 575 vs 1,329)
candidates.angle: 'Can Ozempic affect your nails?' Survey, self-reported, not proven causation. Possible links: rapid weight loss and lower nutrient intake. When to see a dermatologist. Pair with the nutrition theme.
candidates.why_now: Seen in 3 snapshots (66→70→64). Newser picked it up again on Oct 5. It's plateauing, so publish fast or skip.

evidence.signal: GLP-1 Users Report More Nail Detachments (Oct 5)

candidates.topic: Orforglipron (Foundayo) vs insulin glargine in The Lancet: heart-event non-inferiority (4.2% vs 5.0%, HR 0.84) plus 8.9% more weight loss and far less serious low blood sugar (6.8% vs 19.2%) in 2,749 adults with T2D at higher CV risk (ACHIEVE-4)
candidates.angle: Carousel/long follow-up to our 10-01 Short, focused on the practical win: 'A GLP-1 pill vs insulin: what changes day to day?' (hypos, weight, A1C −0.50 points). Report the nominal all-cause mortality HR 0.43 as not multiplicity-controlled. Superiority not shown for 3-point MACE. GI events 62.1%, open-label, Lilly-funded.
candidates.why_now: Pharmacy Times, Cardiovascular Business and Medical Dialogues covered it on Oct 5–6. The 'Can GLP-1 patients stop insulin?' question (Medscape, seen 2×) links in, but never give switching advice.

evidence.signal: ACHIEVE-4 phase 3 CV safety of orforglipron vs insulin glargine
Orforglipron shows CV safety vs insulin glargine
Company results summary

candidates.topic: Is retatrutide approved yet? Lancet TRIUMPH-2 data, Lilly's plans, and why 'research peptide' retatrutide sold online isn't the trial drug
candidates.angle: Attributed-correction format (our 42-view formula): 'Retatrutide isn't approved as of Oct 2026: here's what's real.' Cover the peer-reviewed trial results (20.8% on 12 mg vs 4.0% placebo at 80 weeks, adults with obesity + T2D), the regulatory status (hedged by date), and the regulators' warnings (Philippines FDA advisory on unregistered tirzepatide; 900+ illegal posts in Korea). Never name or point to sources.
candidates.why_now: Many search-query signals ('retatrutide approval status 2026', 'is retatrutide a weight loss drug', 'fda concerns unapproved glp-1 drugs retatrutide'). The Lilly CEO called it the next growth driver (Oct 4). Coverage of illegal and unregistered products in Korea and the Philippines (Oct 6).

evidence.signal: TRIUMPH-2 phase 3 in adults with obesity and T2D
900+ illegal online posts for Mounjaro and Wegovy found

candidates.topic: Teens on GLP-1s and nutrition: 16.88% of 2,031 patients aged 10–17 got a nutritional-deficiency diagnosis within a year of starting (vitamin D 12.4%); only 23.3% had a nutrition visit within 180 days (Childhood Obesity) + prescriptions for ages 8–11 rising fast (Pediatrics)
candidates.angle: 'Parents ask: what should my teen eat on a GLP-1?' Supportive, not alarmist. Claims data shows diagnoses, not proof the drug caused them. Make the case for nutrition counselling. Note that some GLP-1s are approved from age 12. Fact-checker must confirm the exact units in the Pediatrics prescription-rate figures before any number is used.
candidates.why_now: News4JAX/KCRA/Yahoo covered it Oct 4–5, the AAP Pediatrics paper is out, and STAT has an op-ed. Audience fit is secondary (parents within our 25–65 adults).

evidence.signal: Children taking GLP-1s can be at risk of nutritional deficiencies
Trends in GLP-1 RA prescriptions for children ages 8–11 with obesity, 2019–2026
GLP-1 use among young children remains rare but rising rapidly

candidates.topic: GLP-1 after childbirth: postpartum starts rose ~24-fold (0.08% to 1.9%, 2018–Q1 2025) in privately insured US mothers; breastfeeding safety data still limited (JAMA)
candidates.angle: 'Starting semaglutide or tirzepatide after having a baby: what new moms should ask.' Population: privately insured US deliveries. The breastfeeding data gap. Gestational diabetes follow-up. Questions to take to your clinician. No shaming of 'baby weight'.
candidates.why_now: Seen in 2 snapshots (70→68). New angle Oct 5: 44.8% of starters with no pre-delivery diagnosis had none recorded anywhere (Insurance Business). Pairs with the pregnancy meta-analysis.

evidence.signal: GLP-1 prescriptions for new mothers have increased sharply (Oct 1)
Most postpartum GLP-1 starters had no qualifying diagnosis

candidates.topic: What happens after stopping semaglutide or tirzepatide: what the trials show about weight regain (STEP 1 extension, SURMOUNT-4) and the 3-year SURMOUNT-1 prediabetes extension
candidates.angle: Evergreen search magnet ('what happens when you stop Ozempic', Yahoo, Oct 6). Present the trial results neutrally, explain why obesity is treated as a chronic condition, and which habits help hold results. Never advise stopping, switching or tapering: 'make any changes with your prescriber'.
keywords: what happens when you stop Ozempic
candidates.why_now: Yahoo Creators ran a doctor explainer on Oct 6. The Obesity Pillars SURMOUNT-1 3-year analysis gives a fresh hook, and the WashU veterans stopping study (seen 5×, peaking) keeps demand high.

evidence.signal: Weight nadirs and regain over 3 years of tirzepatide in obesity/overweight + prediabetes
What happens when you stop taking Ozempic? (Oct 6)

candidates.angle: Do not produce. Microdosing and self-titration protocols are explicitly banned for the channel, and the trend often relies on compounded or gray-market supply. If ever touched, it can only be a general 'why dosing is set by your prescriber' myth-correction with no protocol detail, and only after editorial sign-off.
candidates.why_now: Mainstream explainer published Oct 6; the trend is circulating on social.

evidence.signal: Microdosing GLP-1s like Ozempic is everywhere
